CB Christian Benford is Questionable [ic5] with a wrist injury but is fully practicing, with an 85.6% snap share [ic6] over 8 games [ic7]. MIA C Aaron Brewer is Out [ic9] with a concussion, and he has logged 8 games of snaps [ic11], so the interior line needs a replacement. WR Jared Wayne is Out [ic12] with a quad injury. WR Chris Bell is Doubtful [ic13] with a knee injury and draws 10.8% of targets [ic16] on 232 team targets [ic17], so his looks go to MIA's remaining receivers if he sits.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: The run game favors BUF: MIA's ground attack has produced -0.11 EPA per run play [mc1] on 214 plays [mc2], while BUF holds opponents to -0.05 [mc3] on 195 plays [mc4] with 6.8 defenders in the box [mc5]. Use the run only to keep the box honest for play action. Against the blitz, which comes on 35.6% of dropbacks [mc6] with a 20.3% pressure proxy [mc7], the interior needs help after Brewer's absence, since he played 100.0% of snaps per game [mc8] over 8 games [mc9]. Get the ball out quickly, use hot throws, and keep a back or tight end in to chip. Explosive passing meets third down: BUF produces explosive pass plays on 12.9% of attempts [mc10] over 295 plays [mc11] against MIA's 0.16 EPA per pass play allowed [mc12], and BUF goes to the pass on 74.3% of third downs [mc13] over 101 plays [mc14], so MIA's rush and coverage must win those downs. In kick coverage, BUF returners average 27.6 yards [mc15] versus MIA's 31.2 yards allowed [mc16], so kick away from the returner and keep lanes tight.
